item.text: {"chapter_id":"6B","issues":[{"question_id":"6B.1","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0038-E001","BATCH-0049-E006"],"explanation":"The answer calls the commitments funded and partly implemented, but E001 is an abstract and E006 establishes planned 2023 budget allocations, not execution or delivery."},{"question_id":"6B.1","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0054-E006"],"explanation":"The answer does not cite direct 2023 evidence that health-and-medicines funding fell 35%, health received unclear targeting, and only 69% of priority programs had results orientation, all material qualifications to claimed welfare priority."},{"question_id":"6B.2","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E001","BATCH-0048-E002","BATCH-0041-E003"],"explanation":"The answer mentions low and inequitable education spending but omits the specific 2023 education-budget and early-childhood allocation evidence, including regressive higher-education spending and insufficient public early-childhood provision."},{"question_id":"6B.2","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0032-E006"],"explanation":"The claim that access improvements were substantial in transfers, pensions, minimum wages, and food security overstates the cited evidence: the supplied items establish outcomes for pensions and selected deprivations, not minimum-wage service access or broad effective uptake."},{"question_id":"6B.3","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0015-E004"],"explanation":"The answer describes migrant-child protection rules and Indigenous consultation requirements as enacted and funded protection, but these citations establish legal or institutional measures and do not show funding sufficiency, enforcement, or actual incidence."},{"question_id":"6B.3","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E013","BATCH-0054-E004","BATCH-0054-E003"],"explanation":"The answer says women and other groups remained disadvantaged but omits direct evidence on gendered labor, food, social-security, and income gaps and on municipal mismatch between pension/disability coverage and local poverty."},{"question_id":"6B.4","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0015-E004"],"explanation":"The statement that some capacity expanded is not demonstrated by the cited evidence; E004 describes formal migrant-child institutions, while E006 is an interpretive account of weakened professional capacity rather than evidence of expanded qualified staffing."},{"question_id":"6B.4","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E006"],"explanation":"The answer gives substantial weight to formal professional and procurement controls but does not clearly preserve that these were only rules with no supplied 2023 audit findings, indicator results, or resolved complaints."},{"question_id":"6B.5","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E003","BATCH-0013-E007","BATCH-0054-E007"],"explanation":"The answer foregrounds CONEVAL's large evaluation output as measurement capacity, but these are largely self-reported institutional outputs and do not establish executive publication of credible service data, independent evaluation use, or correction of failure."},{"question_id":"6B.5","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E008"],"explanation":"The answer mentions unclear populations and indicators but omits the concrete 2023 findings that three of sixteen programs lacked adequate target definitions, 19% lacked clear target populations, and two lacked coverage indicators."},{"question_id":"6B.6","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0014-E016"],"explanation":"The answer presents preparedness mechanisms and emergency exercises as evidence for the 2023 period, although E010 concerns 2019–2022 exercises and E016 mainly concerns 2021 legal measures with no verified 2023 implementation."},{"question_id":"6B.6","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E011","BATCH-0015-E012","BATCH-0015-E015"],"explanation":"UN-supported shelter, education, health, and recovery outputs are treated as evidence of governmental crisis response without adequately weighting that delivery was substantially by UN agencies, civil society, private actors, and subnational partners."},{"question_id":"6B.6","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E009","BATCH-0050-E010"],"explanation":"The answer mentions El Bosque and Otis but omits the specific evidence of prolonged homelessness, lack of food and water in the temporary shelter, poor residents receiving little Otis assistance, and shortages of essential supplies."},{"question_id":"6B.7","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E001","BATCH-0051-E003"],"explanation":"The answer treats courts, CNDH, CONEVAL, and independent evaluators as avenues supplying remedies, but these citations establish monitoring, complaints, or formal protections, not successful appeal outcomes or remedial compliance."},{"question_id":"6B.7","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0021-R01-E014"],"explanation":"The answer broadens migrant, Indigenous, critics, feminists, journalists, and defenders' treatment into a claim about welfare allocation and presidential practice, although the cited evidence concerns institutional violations and CNDH findings without personal presidential ordering or proof of partisan allocation."},{"question_id":"6B.8","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E013","BATCH-0021-R01-E010","BATCH-0041-E004"],"explanation":"The answer appropriately qualifies attribution late, but its opening characterization of 'meaningful formal rights advances' risks crediting the president for reforms enacted by Congress, courts, autonomous bodies, treaty processes, and partners."},{"question_id":"6B.8","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E011","BATCH-0054-E004","BATCH-0046-E007"],"explanation":"The answer omits direct evidence of low compliance with accessibility and Indigenous-rights recommendations, persistent gendered income and food gaps, and the president's reassignment of the Segalmex director despite the governance scandal."},{"question_id":"6B.9","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E006"],"explanation":"The answer describes IMSS-BIENESTAR as supplying authority, indicators, audits, training, complaint systems, and evaluation, but the citations establish prescribed mechanisms only, not reliable funding, professional staffing, transparent operation, or resilience."},{"question_id":"6B.9","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0052-E017"],"explanation":"The answer mentions health-system transitions but does not sufficiently foreground the 2023 fall in health-and-medicines funding, the sharp health-access deterioration, and failure to implement integrated state health networks after policy changes."},{"question_id":"6B.10","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0054-E002"],"explanation":"The answer says ordinary people ended the supplied period with the listed multidimensional and health outcomes, but the principal poverty and health indicators end in 2022; only labor-poverty and income evidence directly reaches 2023."},{"question_id":"6B.10","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0049-E003","BATCH-0054-E002"],"explanation":"The claim that minimum wages rose substantially and produced genuine life-chance gains is only partly supported: the cited evidence establishes wage policy and labor-income changes, not durable population-wide life-chance improvement attributable to the ruler."},{"question_id":"6B.10","issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0053-E010","BATCH-0054-E003","BATCH-0048-E013"],"explanation":"The synthesis omits decisive distributional evidence: extreme-poverty burdens among Indigenous people, children, women, and disabled people; persistent high-lag localities; and worsening gendered access and income disparities."}],"overall_assessment":"The ten answers generally preserve mixed evidence and acknowledge lagged outcomes, shared attribution, and formal-versus-implementation distinctions. Material weaknesses remain: several formal rules, budgets, evaluation outputs, and partner-delivered programs are weighted as evidence of actual welfare performance; some claims exceed what their cited evidence establishes; direct 2023 evidence is intermittently mixed with 2021–2022 or post-period material; and several decisive 2023 budget, targeting, education, health, gender, and distributional counterpoints are omitted or underweighted."}
